title: Enoch walked with God (Genesis 5:21–24)
hook: one line in a list of names: he walked with God, and he was not

segments.voice: Yesterday, Cain and Abel, a jealousy in a field and a question, and your line was you are your brother's keeper. Did you check on a brother or sister? Day three hundred forty-two.

Genesis chapter five is the kind of page most readers skim. It's a family tree, and it has a rhythm like a drum. So-and-so lived this many years, and had a son. And lived this many more years, and had sons and daughters. And all his days were this many years. And he died. Adam, and he died. Seth, and he died. Enosh, and he died. Again and again, name after name, the same ending. Since the garden, the story has been heading here: unto dust shalt thou return. And then, seventh in the line from Adam, the drum skips a beat.
screen: `A FAMILY TREE LIKE A DRUM.` → `AND HE DIED. AND HE DIED.` → `THE DRUM SKIPS A BEAT.`

segments.voice: Here's the line, in the King James Bible: "And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him." That's nearly all we're told. Enoch has a son, Methuselah, who becomes the longest-lived man in the Bible's lists. Enoch himself lives three hundred sixty-five years, a short life by the standards of this chapter. Some readers notice that's the number of days in a year. And instead of and he died, his entry ends: he was not, for God took him. Where did he go? Genesis doesn't say. The letter to the Hebrews says he was taken up so that he should not see death. Later Jewish writings, especially the book of First Enoch, imagined his journeys through the heavens; that book is quoted in the New Testament letter of Jude, and the Ethiopian Orthodox Church counts it as scripture, while most other churches don't. But the verse itself puts the weight on the walk, not the leaving. Walked with God. The Hebrew verb is a form that means walking around, going about, living your daily life with someone, not marching to a destination. It's the language of company. The same phrase will be used of Noah in a few chapters. And it's a picture Christians have loved: not a single dramatic moment, but years of ordinary days, side by side. Methuselah's father, in the middle of a list of deaths, is remembered for one thing: the way he walked. The story doesn't tell us what he said, or did, or built. Just who he walked with.
screen: `HE WAS NOT; FOR GOD TOOK HIM.` · `THREE HUNDRED SIXTY-FIVE YEARS.` · `WHERE DID HE GO?` · `A WALK, NOT A MARCH.` · then, large: `AND ENOCH WALKED WITH GOD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take a slow walk, as prayer. If you can, stand up and walk slowly, around the room, down a hallway, or just in place. If you can't, imagine the walk as you sit. Slower than usual. Feel each foot land. Don't walk to get anywhere. Walk the way you'd walk beside a friend you love, matching their pace. If you pray, you can imagine walking with God, saying nothing. If you don't, just keep the slow company of your own steps. The bell holds the time.
Enoch walked with God. One line in a list of names, where everyone else's entry ends and he died, and his ends with a walk.
Your line: walk with god. Today, take one walk slowly on purpose, even just to the car or the mailbox, and notice who you're keeping company with. Day three hundred forty-two.

howItsDone: Many Christians speak of their faith as a walk with God, and practices like prayer walks, pilgrimages and walking a labyrinth are kept in many churches today.

original.note: Hebrew: Enoch, a name often linked to a root meaning dedicate or train, the same root as Hanukkah.

trapdoor: what you thought: Enoch is a mysterious man who never died.
what it means: in a list of deaths, one man is remembered for a lifetime of walking with God.
what a scholar hears: the Hebrew verb means walking about, daily company, not a march; the same phrase is used of Noah; later writings like First Enoch grew from these four verses.

notes: Enoch is seventh from Adam (Jude 14 says so); Methuselah 969 years (5:27), the longest in the lists. Confirm.
Enoch's 365 years = days in a solar year; script says 'some readers notice'. Confirm.
The verb hithallekh (hitpael of halakh) glossed as 'walking about, going about'; confirm.
1 Enoch in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo canon; quoted in Jude 14–15. Confirm.
Enoch's name linked to the root ch-n-k (dedicate/train), as in Hanukkah; marked 'often linked'. Confirm.
